tagline: Eleven miles under the oaks, and three centuries beside the river.
intro: North from the Church Creek bridge, SC 61 narrows to two lanes and keeps beside the Ashley River for eleven miles under large oaks. State law keeps billboards off it. The federal byway notes allow twenty-five minutes to drive it, or two days to see what is along it.

What is along it is a National Register historic district, the old river country west of the Ashley where planters built houses and gardens and enslaved Africans from rice-growing regions built the dikes and dams of the rice fields. A colonial church, a Palladian house and the oldest landscaped gardens in the country all front the same road.

moments.title: Old St. Andrew's Parish Church
moments.text: Built in 1706 and the oldest surviving church building south of Virginia. Its early vestry once nailed the windows shut and locked the door to keep their own rector out.

moments.title: Drayton Hall
moments.text: The house turns its double portico toward the road rather than the river, and it is the only plantation house on the Ashley to come through both the Revolution and the Civil War intact.

moments.title: Middleton Place
moments.text: Union soldiers burned the house in 1865 and the 1886 earthquake toppled its walls. From 1916 descendants rebuilt the gardens, where six turf terraces step down to a pair of lakes by the river.
